name: MV140
question: Does sublingual MV140 for three or six months reduce culture-confirmed recurrent urinary tract infections compared with placebo in women?

arms.label: Three months of sublingual MV140 followed by three months of placebo

design.population: Women aged 18–75 years in Spain and the United Kingdom with at least five uncomplicated cystitis episodes in the preceding year.
design.locator: Primary PDF pp2–3, Figure 1; phase 3 in secondary report, PubMed abstract, Methods

verdictNote: Both MV140 schedules reduced the prespecified nine-month UTI count versus placebo.
takeaway: Three or six months of sublingual MV140, compared with placebo, reduced the median number of culture-confirmed UTIs during the nine-month efficacy period from 3.0 to 0.0 in women with recurrent uncomplicated cystitis (P<0.001 for each comparison).

reports.label: Primary efficacy and safety
reports.citation: Lorenzo-Gómez MF, Foley S, Nickel JC, et al. "Sublingual MV140 for Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections." *NEJM Evid.* 2022;1(4):EVIDoa2100018. doi:10.1056/EVIDoa2100018
reports.followUp: 12 months from randomization; prespecified efficacy period months 4–12

results.measure: Median episodes (interquartile range) during the nine-month efficacy period

effect.p: <0.001 for each MV140 arm versus placebo

results.note: Protocol-defined primary analysis: 70, 69, and 76 women in the three-month, six-month, and placebo arms; UTI required symptoms and culture ≥10³ CFU/mL; no formal active-duration comparison was planned.
results.locator: Primary PDF pp5,8, Table 2 and Figure 2A

results.measure: Culture-confirmed UTI-free during the nine-month efficacy period
results.note: Prespecified secondary endpoint; a formal success threshold was not stated for this comparison.
results.locator: Primary PDF pp5,8, Table 2 and Figure 2C

results.note: The article's narrative reports the placebo interquartile upper bound as 189 days; Table 2 prints 89 days.
results.locator: Primary PDF p5, Efficacy; p8, Table 2

results.measure: Median episodes (interquartile range) during the whole 12-month study
results.note: Descriptive whole-study comparison in the protocol-defined primary analysis population.

harms.label: Adverse events
harms.note: 205 events in 101 participants; Table 3 reports participants with any event as 34, 28, and 39, respectively. Its placebo safety denominator conflicts with the narrative.

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: Seven serious events occurred in five participants; investigators judged none related to MV140, and no deaths occurred.

delivery.label: Sublingual schedule
delivery.value: MV140 contained heat-inactivated whole cells of E. coli, K. pneumoniae, E. faecalis, and P. vulgaris; two sprays under the tongue daily; the three-month MV140 arm then switched to placebo for three months, and all arms were followed to month 12 with visits every three months; episode antibiotics were permitted.

delivery.label: Treatment and analysis populations
delivery.value: 240 randomized (80 per arm); 229 initiated treatment; 215 completed week 12 and entered the protocol-defined primary analysis; 193 completed the 12-month study.
delivery.locator: Primary PDF pp3,5, Figure 1B and Trial Participants

delivery.label: Treatment adherence
delivery.value: 87% completed the six-month treatment period; adherence did not differ between groups.

reports.label: Personal burden analysis
reports.citation: Nickel JC, Foley S, Yang B, et al. "Reducing Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections in Women with MV140 Impacts Personal Burden of Disease: Secondary Analyses of a Randomized Placebo-controlled Efficacy Study." *Eur Urol Open Sci.* 2024;63:96-103. doi:10.1016/j.euros.2024.03.010

results.measure: Mean days on antibiotics (standard deviation) during months 0–12
results.note: Three-month MV140 (n=74) versus placebo (n=76) in this secondary analysis.

results.measure: Mean total symptom score during UTIs over months 0–12 (standard deviation)
Between-arm difference in total SF-36 change from baseline over months 0–12
results.note: Three-month MV140 versus placebo; secondary analysis of quality-of-life domains.
